GD: layers
The board behind the surface
The board inside your cabinet decides how long it lasts.
Every shelf, shutter and drawer carries weight, day after day.
Common industry practice uses a mix of board types (BWR, MR, MDF, particle board, paper-foil board) and the grade is often not stated.
ISI-certified BWP / HDHMR E0 double-side post-laminated boards are used as the core material in every carcass.
Which board do you use for the carcass, and is it certified?
assets/home5/w7-5.webp
Core board
drop
Moisture, and the 72-hour boiling test
Kitchens and bathrooms are damp, hot and wet places.
Steam, spills and wall dampness reach your furniture every day.
Boards that are not water-tested can swell and weaken over time.
Every BWP-grade plywood is tested in boiling water for 72 hours, with results recorded before it is used in projects.
Can you show me the water-test results for this board?
assets/home5/w7-8.webp
Moisture resistance
wind
Healthy indoor air
What your furniture is made of is part of the air at home.
Wardrobes, kitchens and beds are in your rooms around the clock.
Boards differ in what they release into the room, and many vendors do not say which grade they use.
Core boards are E0 grade, with no formaldehyde, in all carcasses.
What emission grade are your boards, and can you show it in writing?
assets/home/living-room.jpg
Everyday living
award
Certified and tested
Certificates and test records are how you check a promise.
A claim about quality is only as good as the record behind it.
Many vendors give no clarity on which tests were done or what the results were.

ISI-certified boards, and an in-house material testing lab at our factory. Each material is tested twice: when it reaches the factory and when it is issued to a project. We can provide tested samples of the core materials.
Which tests do you run, and can I see a tested sample?
assets/home5/w7-1.webp
Material checks
frame
Sealed edges
Edge bands protect the core board from water and wear.
Wiping, steam and splashes meet the edges of every panel.
Conventional EVA glue applied by hand on ordinary machines may not give the same water resistance and bond strength.
Edge-banding on advanced IMA machines with PUR hot-melt glue. “Peel-off” tests every 2 hours on the lines, with edge strength above 7 Newtons.
How are the edges banded, and how is the bond tested?
assets/home5/guide-tile.webp
Edge-banding detail
glue
The glue you never see
Different parts of your furniture need different bonding systems.
Heat and steam from the kitchen, water splashing on it while cleaning, and years of everyday use affect the quality of furniture.
Poor bonding can lead to laminate lifting, bubbling, or edges coming loose.
Henkel D3 adhesive for laminate pressing, and PUR hot-melt glue for machine edge-banding and specified lamination – ideal for high-temperature environments like kitchens, withstanding up to 80° C.
“What adhesive do you use for pressing, and what for edge-banding?”
assets/home5/guide-06.webp
Edge-banding detail
tool
Hardware and joints
Hinges, runners and dowels do the moving and the holding.
Doors and drawers open and close many times a day.
Materials and accessories are often not tested.
A drawer and shutter cycle test for the durability of runners and hinges, and a compression test for the strength of the board and the load-bearing capacity of the dowel.
How do you test hinges, runners and joints?
assets/home5/w7-6.webp
Joints and fittings
box
Double-carcass boxes
How a cabinet box is built decides how it carries weight and how it can be repaired.
Kitchen tops and loft units hold a lot of weight.
Many major players use a single-carcass system to reduce costs, which can compromise quality and the weight-bearing capacity of the kitchen top.
A double-carcass system on every project, so a single unit can be replaced easily without disturbing the other cabinets.
Is the carcass single or double, and can one unit be replaced on its own?
assets/home5/why-photo.webp
Cabinet construction
scratch
Scratches and finish
Surface finishes need to cope with daily wear.
Pots, bags, keys and cleaning all touch your surfaces.
Many vendors give no information on scratch-resistance testing.

A scratch-resistance test on acrylics, laminates and foils. Acrylic is passed through the flat lamination line with PUR hot-melt glue, with an ABS backer of the same thickness and density on the back of the board.
Do you test scratch resistance, and what backer is used on acrylic?
assets/home5/fan-lamination.webp
Surface finish
grid
Factory-made precision
Where your furniture is made decides how precise it is.
Fitting is smoother when parts are cut and finished to the millimetre.
Many vendors depend on facilities owned by others, and do most of the work on site, which disturbs the home and can compromise quality.
Our own manufacturing facility with CNC and flat-lamination machinery imported from Italy and Germany. Site carpentry is kept for fillers, end panels and visible panels.
Who makes my furniture, and where?
assets/home5/w7-2.webp
In our factory
bars
Strength and load
Furniture has to carry real loads for years.
Shelves, tops and legs are loaded every day.
Vendors often give no clarity on strength testing.
A vertical force test for the load-bearing capacity of a panel, and a leg-strength test to find the breaking point of the leg.
How do you test load capacity and leg strength?
assets/home/factory-cnc.jpg
Load testing
gap
The 18mm gap from the wall
Walls hold dampness, and cabinets should not touch it.
Damp walls are common, especially on outer walls and in wet areas.
Most industry practice leaves no gap, so the carcass touches the wall and exposes plywood to moisture, reducing durability.
An 18mm gap between the wall and the carcass keeps the core materials away from wall dampness, so the product lasts longer.
Is there a gap between my cabinets and the wall?
assets/home/installation.jpg
Installation
palette
Range of finishes
The finish is what you see and touch every day.
Texture and colour set the mood of every room.
A narrow range can limit your design.
Lamination, membrane, acrylic and PU paint, in a wide range of designs, colours and finishing options for every room in your home.
Which finishes can I choose from, and can I see samples?
assets/home5/w7-3.webp
Finish samples
home
Customized for your family
Factory-made does not have to mean standard-sized.
Every home and every family stores and lives differently.
Standard sizes can leave gaps and awkward corners.
Furniture is designed around your room dimensions, storage needs and chosen finishes, with the design and measurements confirmed before production.
Will it be designed around my room and my storage needs?
assets/home/kitchen-l-shaped.jpg
Made for your space
tag
Module-wise pricing
How you are quoted decides how clear the cost is.
Each space needs specific materials, hardware and accessories, and costs differ from module to module.
Most vendors quote a square-foot price, which offers no clarity on the cost of materials and accessories and can lead to higher prices during completion.
Module-wise pricing, so the quotation is as close as possible to the final cost.
Can you give me a module-wise quote?
assets/home5/w7-4.webp
Clear quotes
check
The final quality check
A project should be checked before it reaches your home.
Small faults are easier to fix at the factory than in your living room.
Without a defined check, faults can reach site.
Every project goes through our quality checks before handover, backed by our in-house testing lab and 10-year warranty.
What is checked before my project is handed over?
assets/home/materials.jpg

KL.name: L-Shaped
KL.blurb: Two adjoining walls meet at a corner to free up the centre of the room — the most requested layout for Indian homes because it works in almost any footprint.

pros.b: A tight work triangle between hob, sink and fridge means less walking for the same amount of cooking.
No cabinetry runs through the middle of the room — ideal if you want a breakfast table or open floor.
Works as a compact corner kitchen or a full family kitchen, in the same basic shape.
A single uninterrupted wall makes it simple to plan a window and chimney together.

KL.name: U-Shaped
KL.h1:
Three walls of worktop.
Zero wasted reach.
KL.blurb: Three connected walls of cabinetry give you the most storage and counter space of any layout — built for households that cook often, and together.

pros.b: Three connected walls give more counter and cabinet length than any other layout of the same room size.
Prep, cook and clean each get their own wall, so nothing competes for the same counter.
Naturally closes the kitchen off from the rest of the home — useful for Indian cooking and its aromas.
Wide enough for two people to work at once without getting in each other's way.

KL.name: Galley
KL.blurb: Worktops face each other across a single walkway — the fastest layout to cook in, and the smartest use of a narrow room.

pros.t: The fastest kitchen to cook in
pros.b: Everything sits within arm's reach across a single walkway.
Makes full use of rooms as tight as 6–8 ft wide, where other layouts would not fit.
Hob, sink and storage all sit on one of two facing walls.
Least cabinetry required for the storage you actually get.

KL.name: One-Wall
KL.blurb: Every function lines up along a single wall — the layout of choice for studios and homes that want the kitchen to open into the living room.

pros.b: Everything lines up on one wall, leaving the rest of the space free for living.
One run of plumbing and electrical keeps installation fast and predictable.
Add a freestanding counter later without disturbing the working wall.
Fewer cabinet runs mean a lower starting cost without cutting corners on quality.

KL.name: Peninsular
KL.blurb: An L-shaped layout extended with a connected peninsula — extra counter and seating without the floor space a full island needs.

pros.b: Get extra seating without giving up floor area the way a full island would.
The peninsula visually separates the kitchen from an open-plan living room.
A dedicated counter for serving food and setting down groceries.
Guests can sit at the counter while you cook, instead of standing in the doorway.

KL.name: Island
KL.h1:
Room to gather,
right in the kitchen.
KL.blurb: A freestanding counter sits at the heart of the room — for larger homes that want the kitchen to be where everyone ends up.

pros.b: The island can be a chopping station, a breakfast bar, or both.

pros.t: The social centre of the home
pros.b: Turns cooking into something everyone gathers around, not a room apart.
Add a hob, a sink or just seating to the island face — your call.
Needs more floor area than other layouts, so it suits villas and bigger 4BHKs best.
